minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 3, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley at 5:05 p.m., on September 3, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 28, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Absent:  Mayor Reardon

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Subdivision (a) of Section
  54956.9 City of Mission Viejo adv. Capistrano Unified School District; Settlement
  Agreement terms and conditions.
City Council Minutes  1  September 3, 2013
 CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: 3 potential cases.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The
City Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Mayor Reardon
was absent.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council had time to address only one of the
matters and the remaining item will be continued to a future Council Meeting. Mr. Curley noted
that the Council gave direction to staff, requested additional information, continued the
discussion to a future meeting, and took no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Advanced Meter Outreach Presentation by Southern California Gas Company

  The City Council received the presentation from Emily France, Public Affairs Manager,
  and Paul Simonds, Advanced Meter Outreach Manager, from Southern California Gas
  Company.

  Joe Holtzman, M.V.: stated that the Gas Company's Advanced Meters are nothing more
  than Smart Meters and there are problems associated with them. He recommended that
  residents call the Gas Company and request to be placed on a delay list for these devices.

Presentation to Captain Chris Wilson

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented a proclamation to Chris Wilson, who has been promoted to the
rank of Sheriff's Department Captain and will be leaving the City of Mission Viejo.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

David Dickey, M.V.: announced that he will be presenting a free Economic Forum on four
consecutive Thursday evenings, beginning on September 12, 2013, from 7:00 to 8:30 p.m. at the
Murray Community Center. All sessions are free and he invited residents to attend.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed his objection to the proposed expenditure of $1.3 million in park
fees to upgrade the Pavion Park accessible playground. He stated the proposal should be rejected
and scaled back and he compared the Pavion Park project to other local playground upgrades.

City Council Minutes  2  September 3, 2013
 Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed the recent e-waste recycling event and noted that he was
surprised to find out there was a fee to drop off items when it was advertised as a free event.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced that the City will host a Patriots Day event on September 11
with the participation of local Scout troops. She also stated that as a homeowner, she sees
advantages to the Gas Company's Advanced Meters which will allow people to see unexpected
usage spikes and the meters could actually provide a safety measure.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4, 7, and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Reardon

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 19, 2013, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated August 9, 2013 in the Amount of $773,008.36

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Approval of Long-Range Property Management Plan for Successor Agency of the
  Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo

  Adopted Successor Agency Resolution 13-03 Approving the Long-Range Property
  Management Plan, subject to submittal to and review by the Oversight Board and then by
  the Department of Finance pursuant to California Health and Safety Code Section
  34191.5(b).

City Council Minutes  3  September 3, 2013
 6.  South Orange County Integrated Regional Water Management Plan (IRWMP) Update

  Adopted Resolution 13-48 Adopting the 2013 South Orange County Integrated Regional
  Water Management Plan (IRWMP).

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

9.  Review of Council Policy 0300-8 Management and Budget Policies

  City Manager Wilberg recommended that this item be deferred to a future meeting so that
  all five Council Members can be present for the discussion.

  By consensus, the City Council deferred the matter to a future meeting.

NEW BUSINESS

10. La Paz Bridge Rehabilitation and Road Widening Improvements (CIP 756/761)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented a project overview, lane configurations,
  and renderings that depict the road widening improvements.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay discussed civic core
  enhancements and shared renderings of the project when completed.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: encouraged staff to make sure that the sidewalks are wide enough
  to accommodate all of the school children that walk along La Paz Road.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve
  the bid specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject
  project.

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Reardon

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Check Register dated August 16, 2013, in the amount of $1,742,603.87

  Council Member Schlicht noted that she objects to the payment to Sloan Vazquez as listed
  on page 13 of the check register. She feels that Sloan Vazquez provided a poor report, it
  was written with bias, and it was not worth $3,500.

City Council Minutes  4  September 3, 2013
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Reardon

7.  Ordinance for Permanent Zoning of Two Parcels Totaling Approximately 3.93 Acres
  to Be Annexed into the City of Mission From the County of Orange and the City of
  Rancho Santa Margarita (Zone Change ZC2013-20)

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she pulled this item to keep her vote consistent
  for the dog park land swap.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to adopt
  Ordinance 13-298 Adopting Pre-Zoning to Become the Permanent Zoning of Two Parcels
  Totaling Approximately 3.93 Acres to the Annexed into the City of Mission Viejo from the
  County of Orange and the City of Rancho Santa Margarita, California (ZC2013-20.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Reardon

8.  Multiple Call Party Ordinance

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she would like to reject the ordinance as currently
  written and ask the City Attorney to go back to the drawing board. She stated that it would
  be administratively cumbersome to ask the offending party for cost recovery and
  logistically challenging to determine the fee. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley noted that Lt. Wilson
  recommended that instead of a cost recovery measure, there should be a direct fee; for
  example, $250 for the second call for service, $500 for the third call, and $750 for the
  fourth call.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she feels the City's social host ordinance is
  unconstitutional. She announced that 20 years ago her neighbors harassed her about her
  RV and used the police to do it. She asserted that once she came to the City and began
  making public comments, the City began harassing her too. Council Member Schlicht
  further stated that the Sheriff's Department illegally issued her $2,000 in parking tickets and
  the court agreed. She noted that the proposed ordinance is ripe for abuse without criteria or
  guidelines to protect the citizens.

City Council Minutes  5  September 3, 2013
   Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that the League of California Cities should put out boilerplate
  documents for this type of matter and he announced that he doesn't feel the City needs an
  ordinance like this.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to reject the
  2nd reading of the ordinance.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Reardon

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

11. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

12. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Due to Mayor Reardon's absence, the report was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

13. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  The report was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

14. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg noted that he had nothing to report.

City Attorney’s Report

The City Attorney had nothing to report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

15. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  6  September 3, 2013
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness announced that at the next City Council Meeting he would like the
Council to discuss and consider homebuyer Kelsey Lawrence's application for a low-income unit
at the Ridge Community.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht read a quote from Mark Twain: "No country can be well governed
unless its citizens as a body keep religiously before their minds that they are the guardians of the
law, and that the law officers are only the machinery for its execution, nothing more."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he had no comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley discussed her attendance at a recent meeting of the City's Character
Committee which is planning Character Forums for 8th graders, in partnership with the Chamber
of Commerce. The Committee has sent invitations to the principals of all four middle schools
and both Newhart and Los Alisos Middle Schools have committed their participation. Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley announced that the program involves two forums for student volunteers during
which they will consider an ethical dilemma. The Students will break into groups, each with a
mentor, and will discuss the character predicament. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that it is an
exciting concept and one that is modeled after a program put in place by Irvine Chamber of
Commerce. She announced that she will provide updates on the program as she plans to stay
involved. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley noted that Mayor Reardon is absent tonight due to a
family emergency.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon was absent.

City Council Minutes  7  September 3, 2013
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:20 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of her mother, Dorothy Thompson, to
Monday, September 16, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 16, 2013

City Council Minutes  8  September 3, 2013
